stories.title: Document the architecture and cost topology
stories.description: Resolve and document a cost-aware baseline topology for the static frontend, containerized API, registry, blob assets, content delivery, authentication readiness, public ingress protection, environments, and Azure subscription.
acceptanceCriteria: The design maps every issue requirement to a named Azure service and documents the boundaries between the static frontend, API, assets, authentication, and public ingress
The design records cost, scaling, regional, environment, and operational tradeoffs without claiming deployment evidence
The deployment target explicitly names subscription 11213dbd-39fe-46ba-87db-5f5e8c449aed
stories.notes: Selected and documented the Azure Front Door Premium, Azure Static Web Apps Standard, linked Azure Container Apps, Azure Container Registry, private blob storage, authentication, observability, environment, and cost topology in docs/hosting-infrastructure.md. This story performed no Azure deployment and claims no live endpoint evidence.

stories.title: Create modular Bicep and environment parameters
stories.description: Introduce the idempotent Bicep entry point, reusable modules, explicit environment parameter files, naming conventions, regions, tags, and deployment outputs needed by later resource stories.
acceptanceCriteria: Bicep is organized into bounded modules with a documented deployment entry point
Development and production-ready environment values are explicit in committed parameter or configuration files without secret values
Repeated deployment with the same parameters is designed to converge without duplicate resources or portal-only setup
The Bicep command-line interface version and explicit subscription selection are pinned or documented for automation
stories.notes: Added the subscription-scope infra/main.bicep entry point, bounded resource-group and foundation modules, deterministic naming and non-secret output contracts, explicit dev and prod Bicep parameter files, strict linter configuration, and repository tooling pinned to Bicep CLI v0.46.1. Deployment documentation selects subscription 11213dbd-39fe-46ba-87db-5f5e8c449aed for validation, what-if, and create commands with no portal-only steps. Local compilation and lint validation passed; no Azure deployment was performed or claimed.

stories.title: Provision Azure Static Web Apps frontend hosting
stories.description: Add the Azure Static Web Apps module, environment configuration, deployment outputs, and frontend deployment contract for the existing Vite dist output.
acceptanceCriteria: Bicep declares Azure Static Web Apps frontend hosting with environment-aware naming and configuration
Outputs expose the public frontend endpoint and non-secret deployment configuration
Documentation explains how the existing dist output is deployed without asserting that a live endpoint was created
stories.notes: Added an idempotent Azure Static Web Apps Standard module using the deterministic environment name, explicit development and production staging policies, configuration-file updates, and no repository credential or generated workflow. Subscription outputs expose the resource identity, generated hostname, direct HTTPS endpoint, and a non-secret Vite dist publication contract. Infrastructure documentation covers the dist artifact handoff, Microsoft Entra ID/OpenID Connect automation boundary, approved secret references for service-issued publication credentials, and the absence of live deployment evidence. Local Bicep, formatting, lint, policy, Vite build, artifact, and diff validation passed; no Azure deployment was performed or claimed.

stories.title: Provision Azure Container Apps API and Azure Container Registry
stories.description: Add Azure Container Registry and Azure Container Apps modules for a future Docker-based API, including stable endpoint outputs, image configuration, scaling defaults, and environment parameters.
acceptanceCriteria: Bicep declares an Azure Container Registry and an Azure Container Apps environment and application boundary
The API image reference, ingress, scaling, and environment settings are configurable without committed secrets
Outputs expose the stable API endpoint and registry information required by deployment automation
stories.notes: Added bounded Azure Container Registry and Azure Container Apps Bicep modules with environment-aware image, ingress, scaling, allocation, HTTP concurrency, and non-secret settings parameters. Azure Container Registry Basic disables administrative credentials and anonymous pull; a dedicated user-assigned identity receives only AcrPull, while the Container App has a separate system-assigned runtime identity with no data-plane roles yet. Stable registry, image repository, environment, app, endpoint, deployment contract, and identity outputs are non-secret. Development and production use explicit bounded scaling defaults and a digest-pinned public bootstrap image until workload-identity automation publishes the future API image. Bicep, compiled-contract, formatting, lint, policy, build, and diff validation passed; no Azure deployment, image publication, endpoint reachability test, or live deployment evidence was performed or claimed.

stories.title: Provision blob assets and content delivery
stories.description: Add blob storage containers and a cost-aware content delivery layer for game assets, user-facing media, and other static assets, with explicit caching and endpoint outputs.
acceptanceCriteria: Bicep declares blob storage and separates the required asset categories through documented containers or prefixes
A content delivery endpoint fronts blob-hosted assets with an explicit baseline caching policy
Outputs and documentation identify the upload targets and public content endpoint without claiming live upload evidence
stories.notes: Added dedicated private Blob Storage containers for game assets, user-facing media, and other static assets; environment-aware LRS/ZRS redundancy and recovery settings; a publication-only managed identity with GitHub OpenID Connect federation and Storage Blob Data Contributor; and Azure Front Door Premium category routes with system-assigned managed origin authentication, Storage Blob Data Reader, compression, explicit cache durations, upload-target outputs, and public content endpoint outputs. Azure Front Door managed origin authentication currently cannot be combined with Private Link, so the storage endpoint remains network reachable while anonymous and Shared Key authorization are disabled. Bicep, compiled-contract, credential-pattern, formatting, lint, policy, build, and diff validation passed. No Azure deployment, upload, purge, endpoint reachability check, or live evidence was performed or claimed.

stories.title: Make the topology authentication-ready
stories.description: Define the infrastructure configuration and application-facing outputs needed to enable website authentication later without redesigning the frontend, API, or ingress topology.
acceptanceCriteria: The selected authentication integration point and trust boundaries are documented
Bicep exposes non-secret authentication configuration placeholders and outputs needed by the frontend and API
Enabling authentication does not require replacing the selected frontend, API, asset, or public ingress boundaries

stories.title: Protect public ingress from bots and abuse
stories.description: Add the public ingress layer and environment-aware web application firewall, bot protection, and rate-limiting policy that fronts the appropriate public endpoints.
acceptanceCriteria: The public ingress topology identifies which frontend, API, and asset endpoints are protected
Bicep declares baseline web application firewall, bot protection, and rate-limiting configuration
Protection settings are explicit, environment-aware, and documented with cost and operational tradeoffs

stories.title: Add identities, secrets, observability, and cost controls
stories.description: Complete the baseline with managed identities, secure configuration references, logs and metrics, resource tags, scaling limits, retention settings, and budget-conscious defaults.
acceptanceCriteria: Workload access uses managed identities and least-privilege role assignments where supported
Secret values are absent from committed files and the secure runtime injection mechanism is documented
Diagnostics, retention, scaling limits, tags, and cost-aware defaults are explicit and environment-aware
Required operational and application deployment outputs are exposed without revealing secrets

stories.title: Document deployment and end-to-end verification
stories.description: Add repeatable preview, deployment, application publication, asset upload, and end-to-end verification procedures for the complete baseline stack without deploying from the Ralph iteration.
acceptanceCriteria: Documentation selects subscription 11213dbd-39fe-46ba-87db-5f5e8c449aed explicitly and describes preview and idempotent deployment commands
Continuous deployment workflows validate and deploy the Bicep and publish the frontend, API image, and assets using approved secret injection
The verification procedure covers frontend reachability, frontend-to-API access, authentication readiness, asset content delivery, ingress protection, outputs, and repeat deployment
Repository checks validate templates, configuration, and documentation without inventing live Azure acceptance evidence
